hints: Look carefully at the carbonyl group in the skeletal formula and decide if it is at the end of the chain or in the middle.
Count every bend and end in the carbon skeleton to get 7 carbons, then use the ketone general formula $C_nH_{2n}O$ to find the hydrogens.
Recall which type of carbonyl compound reduces Fehling's reagent to give a red precipitate, and which type shows no change.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional group from the structure**

Look at the $C=O$ group. It is joined to two other carbons, one $CH_3$ on the right and one $CH_2$ on the left. That makes it a ketone, not an aldehyde.

$$R-CO-R' \text{ = ketone}$$

**Count carbons to get the molecular formula**

In skeletal formulae each end and bend is a carbon. Counting from the right: $CH_3-C(=O)-CH_2-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$ gives 7 carbons in total. This is 5-methylhexan-2-one.

$$\text{carbon count = 7}$$

**Work out hydrogens and oxygens**

There is one oxygen from the ketone. A saturated acyclic ketone follows $C_nH_{2n}O$, so for $n=7$ we get $C_7H_{14}O$.

$$\text{molecular formula = } C_7H_{14}O$$

**Predict the Fehling's test result**

Fehling's reagent is an oxidising agent that is reduced by aldehydes to red $Cu_2O$, but ketones resist oxidation under these mild conditions. Since X is a ketone, there will be no reaction.

$$\text{aldehyde + Fehling's } \rightarrow \text{ red precipitate, ketone + Fehling's } \rightarrow \text{ no change}$$

options.A: Correct. X has 7 carbons and is a ketone, so its formula is $C_7H_{14}O$. Ketones do not reduce Fehling's reagent, so no change is observed.
options.B: Formula is right but test is wrong. A red precipitate with Fehling's shows an aldehyde. Students choosing this have confused ketones with aldehydes, both contain $C=O$ but only aldehydes are oxidised.
options.C: Test is right but formula is wrong. $C_7H_{16}O$ is the formula for a saturated alcohol or ether. The $C=O$ double bond removes 2 hydrogens, giving $C_7H_{14}O$. This error comes from counting hydrogens as if the compound were saturated with only single bonds.
options.D: Both parts are wrong. $C_7H_{16}O$ ignores the unsaturation from $C=O$, and a red precipitate would require an aldehyde. X is a ketone with the carbonyl in the middle of the chain, so it cannot be oxidised by Fehling's.
